**Proposed mechanism:** PDYN (HGNC:9153) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal enzyme activity (GO:0005704); PSAP (HGNC:9154) —DISRUPTS→ Lysosomal enzyme activity (GO:0005704); Lysosomal enzyme activity (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Spinocerebellar ataxia (HP:0001284); Lysosomal enzyme activity (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Gaucher disease (HP:0003124). Mutations in PDYN (for SCA23) and PSAP (for Gaucher disease) both lead to impaired lysosomal enzyme activity, which in turn results in the distinct phenotypes of spinocerebellar ataxia and Gaucher disease, respectively.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in PDYN and PSAP do not affect common downstream lysosomal pathways or that the observed phenotypes are entirely independent and unrelated to lysosomal function. _(variant: Presence of common, benign variants in PDYN and PSAP in the general population that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on functional lysosomal enzyme activity could inform therapeutic strategies targeting lysosomal dysfunction that might benefit patients with either spinocerebellar ataxia type 23 or Gaucher disease, particularly if enzyme replacement or chaperone therapies can be developed to augment general lysosomal function.
